Very dilute oil droplets can require a **longer coalescence residence time** because when the droplet concentration is low, **droplet–droplet collisions are much less frequent**. Coalescence depends on droplets meeting and merging, so at low oil loading the system needs **more time** for enough collisions to occur.

The **footprint trade-off** in gravity water treatment is that it is **simple and low-energy**, but it typically requires a **large physical footprint**. In other words, you trade **land area** for **passive separation**.
